text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like SPY on 2020-03-16, the median realised 5-session return was 1.36%. The distribution is wide and left-skewed, with a standard deviation of 12.32% and a 10th percentile of -22.12%, meaning the single number to anchor on is that while more than half the analogs recovered over five sessions, the downside tail contained severe drawdowns.

[state]
The engine retrieved these specific episodes because the query state sits at extreme z-scores across almost every feature. The 5-session return was -12.54% (z=-3), the 20-session return was -28.95% (z=-3), and the drawdown from the 60-session peak was -29.11% (z=-3). Simultaneously, 20-session realised volatility hit 78.3% (z=3), the mean absolute overnight gap was 2.78% (z=3), dollar volume was 15.408 standard deviations above normal (z=3), and VIX stood at 82.69 (z=3). Macro features reinforce the shock: WTI crude fell 44.34% over 20 days (z=-3) and the trade-weighted USD rose 3.88% (z=3). The signals block records macro readings from a later measurement date rather than March 2020, so the contemporaneous backdrop is not available on this card for the equity sentiment or news layers; the crypto sentiment reading of 0.09 on the fear & greed index applies only to the separate crypto market and does not describe the equity mood here.

[history]
Across the 50 analogs, the median 5-session forward return was 1.36% with a mean of -2.3% and a standard deviation of 12.32%. The distribution is negatively skewed at -1.141. In 56% of the episodes the return was above zero, and in 44% it was below. The 10th percentile was -22.12% and the 25th percentile was -7.28%, while the 75th percentile was 6.29% and the 90th percentile was 9.37%. The worst outcome was -40.53% and the best was 19.93%. The bad tail is dominated by early-March 2020 industrial and energy names: Boeing (BA) on 2020-03-05 returned -40.53%, ConocoPhillips (COP) on 2020-03-04 returned -34.13%, Morgan Stanley (MS) on 2020-03-05 returned -26.49%, and the Energy Select ETF (XLE) on 2020-03-06 returned -24.26%. The closest match by distance was Caterpillar (CAT) on 2020-03-09 at 0.8076, which returned -10.24%.

[tails]
A position could end near the median and still have been un-holdable during the week. The median max adverse excursion across the 50 analogs was -4.21%, and the 10th percentile of adverse excursion was -22.87%. In 48% of the episodes, the path breached a 5% drawdown at some point during the 5 sessions. A 10% drawdown was breached in 30% of the cases, a 15% drawdown in 18%, and a 20% drawdown in 14%. The median max favourable excursion was 4.68%, giving a reward-to-risk ratio of 1.11.

[stress]
Of the 14 scenarios run, 5 were skipped because their windows ended after the 5-session embargo before 2020-03-16: covid-crash, rate-shock-2022, regional-banks-2023, carry-unwind-2024, and tariff-shock-2025. Among the executed scenarios, the FOMC decision day stress produced the weakest median forward return at -0.52%, a delta of -1.88% versus the baseline, with a 36% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; its caveat is that only 92 decision days exist in the calendar, so the analog set is small and highly overlapping. The earnings release day scenario shifted the median down by -1.3% to 0.06%, widening the 10th percentile to -25.18%; its caveat notes that earnings dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than 8-K Item 2.02 dates. The weekend hold on the 7x24 venue scenario produced a median of 0.96% (delta -0.4%), with a 32% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; its caveat states that blocks are paired to analogs by index modulo the block count as a deterministic convention, not a joint distribution, and that a perpetual carries funding and basis a spot token does not. The vol-spike scenario actually improved the median to 1.87% (delta +0.51%), though the 10th percentile widened to -20.12%; its caveat is that VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, so this stresses entry timing more than terminal value.

[reasoning]
The FOMC decision day scenario matters most because it is the only one that pushed the median into negative territory (-0.52%) and raised the 10% drawdown breach probability to 36% across 50 analogs. The earnings release day scenario is second because it produced the widest left tail (-25.18% at the 10th percentile) and lowered the median by 1.3% against the baseline. The weekend hold 7x24 venue scenario is third because it directly tests the path risk of holding a tokenised wrapper when the reference market is shut, raising the 10% drawdown breach probability to 32%. A reader should distrust the heavy concentration of early-March 2020 Industrials and Energy names in the retrieval set—12 Technology, 9 Industrials, 9 Financials, and 6 Energy analogs out of 50, with 14 from 2020 alone—as they reflect a single correlated liquidity event rather than independent draws. No executed scenario contradicts the direction of a recovery, as all medians except FOMC day remained positive.

[limits]
This analysis has concrete limits. The honest verdict from the validation block states: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." The directional hit rate is 50.1%. For path risk, the engine targets a 10% drawdown breach level. Out of sample, the realised breach rate was 2%, while the mean predicted rate from the analog excursion share was 3.4%, producing a calibration gap of 1.4 percentage points with a clustered standard error of 0.48. The analog Brier score was 0.0196, compared to 0.0241 for the volatility reflection benchmark, 0.024 for the same-name calibration, and 0.021 for the pooled calibration. The paired Brier confidence intervals resolve the analog's superiority over all three benchmarks, as none span zero (vol reflection ci95Low -0.0071, ci95High -0.0022; same-name ci95Low -0.0059, ci95High -0.0029; pooled ci95Low -0.0023, ci95High -0.0005). The wrapper status is measured on the primary venue, Bitget official MCP (agent.bitget.com/mcp), using the SPY/USDT RWA perpetual. The reference cash market is shut for 81.4% of the week, and 61.18% of the wrapper's own hourly movement landed in those closed hours. Tracking is rated fair with a correlation of 0.9477 and a tracking error of 23 bp/day. The basis band is -0.04% to 0.31%, and the spread is 0.13 bps. The wrapper caveat notes that this is a perpetual carrying funding and basis, not a redeemable spot token, and that the upstream API silently ignores granularity parameters, so the echoed interval is checked rather than trusted. For the return layer, across 6 distinct weekend starts, the median weekend block return was -0.101%, the 10th percentile was -0.506%, the standard deviation was 0.4191%, and the median intra-weekend adverse excursion was -0.2125%. Zero percent of those 6 weekends breached the 5% drawdown threshold. These are wrapper returns measured while the reference market was shut and NOT the retrieved outcome distribution above, which is built on 5x24 daily sessions of the underlying.
